transcript: Speaker A: Spelling likhte waqt ye tukka maarna band karo aur English mein ing lagane ka simple rule seekh lo. Jump ke peeche ing lagaya toh jumping hota hai. Par run word ke peeche agar hum ing lagaye toh running. Yaani yahan ek ki jagah n n ho jaate hain. Kabhi socha hai aisa kyun? Chalo iska ek simple rule main aapko samjhati hoon. Jo bhi word hai usme hamesha peeche se letters count karo. Ek, do. Agar do number pe koi vowel aaye yaani ki a, e, i, o, u aur iska agar short sound nikal raha hai toh rule yaad rakho. One, two, double i, do. Yaani aakhri letter ko double karke ing laga do. Isliye run ka running ho jayega aur tap ka... tapping. Lekin agar hum jump ko peeche se count karein toh one, two, three. Yahan vowel teesre number par aa raha hai. Toh iska rule hai, one, two, three, it's not for me. Yaani yahan par double nahi karna hai. Isiliye jump ka bana... jumping. Aur help ka bana... helping. Lekin English ke aise hi hazaaron shortcuts, dimaag khol dene wale rules aur daily use hone wali English aap bina ratte English Seekho app par seekh sakte ho. Yahan par aapko koi boring padhai nahi karni hai. Aap experts ki aise hi short, crisp aur smart videos dekhkar rozana bolne wali English, mushkil grammar rules aur ekdum perfect pronunciation yaani har word ko sahi se bolne ki smart tricks ko seekh sakte hain. Woh aapki har galti ko pakadkar sahi karegi aur aapki English ko ekdum mast aur polish kar degi. Toh ab rules ka ratta maarna band karo, smart tareeqe se videos dekho aur AI coach ke saath farratedar English bolna seekho. Abhi English Seekho app download karo. [Stop guessing spellings and learn the simple rule for adding '-ing' in English. Adding '-ing' to 'jump' makes 'jumping', but adding it to 'run' makes 'running' with a double 'n'. Ever wondered why? Let me explain a simple rule. Always count letters from the back of the word. One, two. If there is a vowel at position two (a, e, i, o, u) with a short sound, remember this rule: 'One, two, double I do'. This means double the last letter and add '-ing'. So 'run' becomes 'running' and 'tap' becomes 'tapping'. But if we count 'jump' from the back: one, two, three. Here, the vowel is at position three. The rule for this is: 'One, two, three, it's not for me'. This means do not double the letter. So 'jump' becomes 'jumping' and 'help' becomes 'helping'.
